characternet.architecture: Dynamic Architecture: connecting load-bearing relationships that fuse the four beams — shape, form, pinyin, tone — and meaning into a single causal scene. Different scene each time, same kind of connection. Remove any beam and recall collapses.

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (one flat line) with the sound 'yī' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'one'.
characters.leading_question: How many lines of sheep?
characters.scene_example: Is that one line of sheep? Yee (yī) — yes!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (two stacked lines) with the sound 'èr' and the 4th falling tone into a scene that means 'two'.
characters.leading_question: Is that two lines of sheep?
characters.scene_example: Eeeer (èr) — yes! Two lines of sheep!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (three stacked lines) with the sound 'sān' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'three'.
characters.leading_question: Is that three lines of sheep?
characters.scene_example: Yes — sandwiched (sān) together! Three lines of sheep!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (an enclosure with legs inside) with the sound 'sì' and the 4th falling tone into a scene that means 'four' — sheep jumping down into the pen.
characters.leading_question: Is that four lines in that opening?
characters.scene_example: Let me jump in to see (sì)! Four lines in the pen!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a gate/fence structure) with the sound 'wǔ' and the 3rd falling then rising tone into a scene that means 'five'.
characters.leading_question: Is that five lines?
characters.scene_example: Wu-ait (wǔ) — yes, five!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a lid over two splayed legs) with the sound 'liù' and the 4th falling tone into a scene that means 'six' — the lid lowers to hide two ears, leaving six visible parts.
characters.leading_question: What happens when you lower a lid on the bah-bah sheep?
characters.scene_example: This sheep is out of line — lower (liù) the lid on its head, hiding its 2 ears — now only 6 parts are visible!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (an upside-down 7 crossed by a cue-stick line) with the sound 'qī' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'seven'.
characters.leading_question: What is the escaped sheep caught with?
characters.scene_example: The sheep is getting away — grab the cue stick (qī)! It looks like an upside-down seven with a cue-stick crossbar through the middle.

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (two splayed legs of a sheep standing front-on) with the sound 'bā' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'eight' — 8 parts: 2 ears, 2 eyes, 2 sets of 2 legs.
characters.leading_question: How many parts has the bah-bah black sheep?
characters.scene_example: A bah-bah (bā) black sheep stands front-on (八) for inspection — 8 parts: 2 ears, 2 eyes, 2 sets of 2 legs!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (leg stroke, one line, curled tail) with the sound 'jiǔ' and the 3rd falling then rising tone into a scene that means 'nine' — the sheep's forgotten tail is the 9th part.
characters.leading_question: What did the sheep forget to have counted?
characters.scene_example: One sheep turns sideways and jiokes (jiǔ): 'You forgot to count my tail — the 9th part!' The shepherds laugh.

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a cross of two lines, like a fallen tent crossbar) with the sound 'shí' and the 2nd rising tone into a scene that means 'ten'.
characters.leading_question: What has fallen on the ground?
characters.scene_example: All sheep accounted for — let's head back. Is that a crossbar on the floor? Shiite (shí) — the sheep tent (ten) has fallen!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a person, and a knife-cut small shape) with the sound 'nǐ' and the 3rd falling then rising tone into a scene that means 'you' — a knee-high small person, that's you.
characters.leading_question: How much is the person cut short?
characters.scene_example: A person (亻) knife-cut (⺈) small (小) — a knee-high (nǐ) short person — that's you!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a woman, a child) with the sound 'hǎo' and the 3rd falling then rising tone into a scene that means 'good' — a woman with her child, how good is that.
characters.leading_question: What is a woman with a child?
characters.scene_example: A woman (女) with her child (子) — how (hǎo) good is that!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a hand, a halberd) with the sound 'wǒ' and the 3rd falling then rising tone into a scene that means 'I, me'.
characters.leading_question: What is the hand doing with the spear?
characters.scene_example: The hand (手) raised in court shouting (shǒu) 'Order!' is the same hand holding a spear (戈) — getting (gē) ready to shoot straight at the people — 'Wow (wǒ) — that's me, I will do that!'

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (sun, moon) with the sound 'míng' and the 2nd rising tone into a scene that means 'bright' — light plus light gives bright light.
characters.leading_question: What is the outcome when sun and moon are together?
characters.scene_example: Sun (日) and moon (月) together — both give light — light plus light gives bright (míng) light!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (woman, horse) with the sound 'mā' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'mother' — a woman called 'Ma' (mama) is a mother.
characters.leading_question: What makes a woman with a horse a mother?
characters.scene_example: A woman (女) with a horse (马) — what makes her a mother? She is called 'Ma' — mama (mā) — a mother!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a person, also) with the sound 'tā' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'he, him' — a male person is also a 'he'.
characters.leading_question: What is a person also?
characters.scene_example: A person (亻) — what is a person also (也)? A male person is also a 'he' (tā)!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a woman, also) with the sound 'tā' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'she, her' — a female person is also a 'she'.
characters.leading_question: What is a woman also?
characters.scene_example: A woman (女) — what is a woman also (也)? A female person is also a 'she' (tā)!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a roof, a curled shape) with the sound 'tā' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'it' — a non-human thing is also an 'it'.
characters.leading_question: What is a thing also?
characters.scene_example: A covered thing (宀 + 匕) — what is a thing also? A non-human thing is also an 'it' (tā)!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (knife-cut, small, lying-down person shape) with the sound 'ěr' and the 3rd falling then rising tone into a scene that means 'you (archaic)' — you, sir, are the knife-cut small person.
characters.leading_question: What has been knife-cut small?
characters.scene_example: Knife-cut (⺈) small (小) — what is cut short? Look again: a person lying down on their side. You, sir (ěr) — you are the knife-cut small person!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (tree, tree) with the sound 'lín' and the 2nd rising tone into a scene that means 'forest' — two trees together make a forest.
characters.leading_question: What do two trees together make?
characters.scene_example: One tree (木), then another tree (木) beside it — together they rise (lín) into a forest!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (tree, tree, tree) with the sound 'sēn' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'dense forest' — three trees make a dense forest.
characters.leading_question: What do three trees together make?
characters.scene_example: Tree (木), tree (木), tree (木) — flat and dense (sēn) — a dense forest!

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a person, a tree) with the sound 'xiū' and the 1st high and flat tone into a scene that means 'rest' — a person leaning on a tree to rest.
characters.leading_question: What is a person doing beside a tree?
characters.scene_example: A person (亻) leans on a tree (木) — 'Shoo (xiū), I'm resting!' — flat and calm.

characters.binding_constraint: Bind the visual pieces (a hand over an eye) with the sound 'kàn' and the 4th falling tone into a scene that means 'to look / watch' — a hand shading the eye to look into the distance.
characters.leading_question: What is a hand doing over an eye?
characters.scene_example: A hand (手) over an eye (目) — 'Can (kàn) you see?' — the hand drops down to look — to look / watch!
